Implement is_balanced(s) so that it returns True when the three kinds of brackets (), [] and {} in the string s are correctly matched and nested, and False otherwise. spec.restated_task: Implement brackets.is_balanced(s) in brackets/core.py to return a bool indicating whether all parentheses, square brackets, and braces in a string are correctly paired and nested. Ignore all other characters, treat the empty string as balanced, and raise TypeError for non-string inputs. Preserve is_bracket, package imports, and existing tests.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Accept a str instance, including subclasses. Consider only the six characters ()[]{}. Each closing bracket must match the most recent opening bracket that has not yet been closed. Return True exactly when every closing bracket matches and no opening brackets remain unmatched; otherwise return False. Return an actual bool. Ignore every other character, including whitespace and Unicode characters. Brackets inside quoted text are still brackets; quoting and escaping have no special meaning.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str, including None, bytes, numbers, and containers. Do not coerce non-string inputs to strings. Exception message is unspecified.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing implementation: return True exactly when c is a str instance of length one and is one of ()[]{}; return False otherwise.

acceptance_criteria: 1. from brackets import is_balanced and from brackets import is_bracket continue to work.
2. is_balanced returns True for each of '', '()', '[]', '{}', '()[]{}', and '([{}])'.
3. is_balanced returns True for nested and adjacent pairs, including '((()))', '[[]]', '{{}}', and '([]){}[()]'.
4. is_balanced returns True for '(a[b]{c})' and 'f(x[0], y[1])'.
5. Strings containing no bracket characters, including ordinary text, whitespace, and Unicode text, return True.
6. Inserting or removing non-bracket characters anywhere does not change the result. Quotation marks and backslashes do not suppress bracket recognition.
7. is_balanced returns False for each of '(', ')', '([)]', '(]', '{[}', and '())'.
8. Unmatched opening brackets of every kind return False, including '[', '{', and '([]'.
9. Unmatched closing brackets of every kind return False, including ']', '}', ')(', '[]]', and '{}('.
10. Every result for a string input has type bool, including both balanced and unbalanced cases.
11. Non-string inputs raise TypeError, including None, True, 0, 1.5, b'()', [], (), {}, and set().
12. Instances of a str subclass are accepted and evaluated using the same bracket rules.
13. Repeated calls are independent: calling with an unbalanced string does not affect a subsequent balanced result.
14. is_bracket remains unchanged and returns True for each of the six bracket characters and False for 'a', '', '((', and 1.
15. Existing test files remain unchanged and their tests continue to pass.
out_of_scope: Changing is_bracket, PAIRS, OPEN, CLOSE, or package exports.
Recognizing additional bracket kinds or adding quotation, escape, or language-parsing rules.
Adding dependencies, new public APIs, or unrelated refactoring.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing ones changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion is never overridden. The classification itself remains a model judgement.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.
